chapter: Navy years and attitudes toward whites
title: Logistics support company and the white company sent first to Okinawa
summary: His all-black unit trained three months but a white company with less training was sent first and nearly wiped out.

blocks.x: We worked, but that's what I was coming to. You see, after we were shipped from Massachusetts, from Boston, to Camp Perry, Williamsburg, Virginia. Now, this is where we made history. We were, see, they dismantled their Seabees, and they came up with this new thing we're called Logistics Support Companies. Now, we were the first in this new organization of logistic support companies. We went to Camp Perry, Williamsburg, Virginia, and we took three months of combat training. I mean, hard, cold combat. So it was a work fight. We had to make sure supplies get there, and when they got on the beach we had to protect them. So we had all of the training that our infantry would have. I mean, now, here's what happened. In order to not give it to blacks, this is something that, you know, in order to not give it to us, they brought a white company in. We took three months training. They brought a white company in, gave them six weeks training. shipped them to Okinawa. A whole company. And you know what? When we finished our training and we got to California, six of them was left out of the company. And companies, like 130-something, I forgot exactly how many, but they were all killed in the third landing on Okinawa. But that was done to keep us from getting that recognition as being the first logistic support company. So, I'm alive. So, you were in all segregated, all black outfits?
Oh yeah, all black outfits. All black outfits.

And, you know, when we left Camp Perry, when we finished our training, you see they changed, they changed our uniform. And then we went to the uniform. Our work uniform went from dungarees to green, fatigue green. Yeah. So, we had the green uniform, kind of like the Marine, with the helmet and boots and everything. And we had all our fighting with rifles. We had a call being, and I called my initial, you know, like we go and fight. Everybody was happy about this. But, like I said, they took this honor away from us. Yes. And so, when we got to California, that's when we met the six people that was back out of the white company that they sent on and they all got killed. So, everybody was saying, well, kind of maybe we're glad because probably we'd be there too, if we had been in that first company. Yeah. So, we went to Okinawa and I can remember my first, when we got to Okinawa, boy, it was a dismal day. Gray, low clouds. So, y'all were finally shipped into combat. Yeah. Oh, well, we were right in the middle of it.
